claims.statement: China's geopolitical risk index in October 2026 stands at 0.84% of newspaper articles, below the recent spike levels but elevated compared to mid-2025.
China experienced a major geopolitical risk spike in March 2026, reaching 1.70% of articles, the highest level since March 2022 and representing a near-tripling from the prior month.
China's geopolitical risk remained elevated through spring 2026, with April and May 2026 showing sustained high levels of 1.66% and 1.73% respectively.
The March 2026 spike coincided with a global geopolitical risk index of 330.18, the second-highest level in the entire dataset after March 2022's 318.95.
China's geopolitical risk has declined from the March-May 2026 peak but remains above the 2024-2025 baseline, with October 2026 at 0.84% versus an average of approximately 0.65% in late 2025.
The historical China GPR index (gprhc_chn) in October 2026 stands at 0.65%, indicating moderate geopolitical risk coverage in the longer-term historical newspaper sample.
China's geopolitical risk showed a sharp drop in June 2026 to 0.85%, falling by more than half from May's 1.73%, suggesting a de-escalation or shift in media focus.
The global GPR index in October 2026 stands at 150.52, significantly elevated above the 1985-2019 baseline of 100 and indicating sustained worldwide geopolitical tensions.

summary: China experienced a severe geopolitical risk spike in March 2026, with newspaper coverage reaching 1.70% of articles, the highest level since March 2022 and coinciding with a global GPR index of 330.18 [geopolitical:CHN:002][geopolitical:CHN:004]. This elevated risk persisted through spring 2026, with April and May maintaining high levels of 1.66% and 1.73% respectively [geopolitical:CHN:003]. The risk profile showed a sharp decline in June 2026, dropping to 0.85% [geopolitical:CHN:007]. As of October 2026, China's geopolitical risk stands at 0.84% of articles, which remains above the late-2025 baseline but well below the spring 2026 peak [geopolitical:CHN:001][geopolitical:CHN:005]. The global GPR index remains elevated at 150.52, indicating sustained worldwide geopolitical tensions [geopolitical:CHN:008]. The historical GPR measure for China shows moderate coverage at 0.65% in October 2026 [geopolitical:CHN:006].
